orbis-porting-kit is MIT-licensed, with ONE named exception. That file says so in its own
header; each file's SPDX-License-Identifier is authoritative for that file.

  cmake/orbis-tls.ld     GPL-3.0-only. It is the OpenOrbis PS4 Toolchain's own link.x (release
                         v0.5.4, asset toolchain-llvm-18.tar.gz) with two match patterns added to
                         the .tls rule. That toolchain is GPL-3.0 and grants no linking exception,
                         so this derivative cannot be relicensed by the person deriving it. It
                         carried an MIT header until 2026-09-17; that header was wrong.

                         ⚠ IT IS ON EVERY CONSUMER'S LINK LINE, and the honest statement of what
                         that means is this: a linker script DIRECTS the linker, it is not linked
                         into the output, so no part of this file ends up in a title built with it.
                         That is the reading; it is not legal advice, and anyone shipping a
                         closed-source title should satisfy themselves rather than take a README's
                         word for it.

  services/              Extracted on 2026-09-18 from orbis-ports/OpenGothic (ps4/og_sound_orbis.cpp,
                         ps4/og_ps4_ime.cpp, ps4/og_ps4_boot.cpp), which is MIT, and written by the
                         same author as this repository. The one piece in those files that was NOT
                         his - an IMA-ADPCM decoder lifted from Tempest, also MIT - was deliberately
                         left behind, because it is a codec rather than a platform service.
